patches.find: writing his Histories around 440 BCE — roughly fifty years after the battle itself.
patches.replace: writing his Histories a few decades after the battle, most likely around 430 BCE.
patches.reason: Fecha habitual de las Historias: c. 430 a. C. (≈50 años después); «around 440» es temprano.

patches.find: Nothing here documents how the Huns' cavalry actually fought in battle. Everything that follows about the Huns is general historical understanding — the kind of picture widely repeated in popular history. It is not something we can point to a cited ancient text for.
patches.replace: Ancient writers did describe the Huns — the Roman historian Ammianus Marcellinus, the envoy Priscus who met Attila in person, and later Jordanes — but always from the outside, often with open hostility, and never with the tactical detail Herodotus gives Thermopylae. So everything that follows about how the Huns would have fought here is informed reconstruction, not a documented account.
patches.reason: Sí existen fuentes antiguas sobre los hunos (Amiano Marcelino, Prisco, Jordanes): hostiles y poco detalladas, no inexistentes. Se conserva la primera frase (acotada al material del video) porque ancla una marca de edición.

patches.reason: Los 300 no derrotaron a nadie (cayeron); la frase original confundía.
